elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The Company may terminate this Agreement at any time for convenience, with or without cause, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to HDI." No Order Forms exist in this hosting agreement, so the Agreement-level right suffices.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted Company right runs on "ninety (90) days' prior written notice", which exceeds the 30-day preferred anchor.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: under Section 3.1 the Company pays HDI 30% of Net Sales in excess of $11,000 per calendar month in arrears, so there are no prepaid fees capable of pro-rata refund. No refund text was added and none is needed.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Any termination by HDI under this Section 4.1 shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term, and any Termination Date specified in HDI's notice shall be the last day of that term." HDI's exit is now term-end only, i.e. non-renewal rather than mid-term convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Standalone operative sentence gives the Company a mid-term convenience right "at any time ... upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice", curing the risk that the 90-day right in the auto-renewal sentence reads only as a non-renewal mechanic.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the amounts payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." Section 3 is the fee/payment provision (30% of Net Sales), so the cap is a real three-months-of-fees ceiling on the otherwise uncapped Net-Sales-less-$800,000 formula.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: HDI's termination is expressly made "effective only at the end of the then-current term" and the defined Termination Date in HDI's notice must be "the last day of that term" — the effective date is tied to term end, as the rule requires.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 4.1: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — already satisfied for HDI; no edit required.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day Company convenience right, three-months-of-fees cap on the Termination Payment, HDI termination effective only at term end, HDI's pre-existing 90-day notice).
Preferred level fails only on the 30-day notice anchor; the pro-rata refund element is inapplicable because fees are paid in arrears as a share of Net Sales, so there are no prepaid fees.

Minimality holds: the redline adds three short sentences, each traceable to a fallback element (clarified Company exit, HDI term-end limitation, fee cap), retains the existing Termination Payment formula and quarterly instalment mechanic rather than deleting favourable or neutral text, and omits surplus such as "in whole or in part". "with or without cause" is redundant with "for convenience" but adds no new obligation.

Intent preserved: the auto-renewal structure, defined Termination Date, Section 3 fee mechanics, and the eight-quarterly-instalment payment schedule all survive without contradiction; the cap cross-reference to Section 3 resolves to a defined payment obligation.

Drafting caution (not a failure): the HDI limitation is drafted as "[a]ny termination by HDI under this Section 4.1". If Section 4.1 also houses an HDI termination-for-cause right in an unquoted sub-paragraph, narrow the sentence to "any termination by HDI for convenience under this Section 4.1" so a for-cause exit is not inadvertently deferred to term end.
